author: Sam Carrico
title: Tulsa teen honored for helping save friend after bike crash at Turkey Mountain - NewsBreak
text:
By Sam Carrico ,
7 hours ago
The Tulsa Fire Department recognized a local teenager on Wednesday for helping save his friend after a bike crash at Turkey Mountain over the summer.
Firefighters said when Emerson Kuykendall’s friend got into a serious bike crash, Kuykendall called for help and guided crews directly to the scene.
Quick thinking on the trails Inside Fire Station 6, 17-year-old Emerson Kuykendall received a Letter of Commendation from Tulsa Fire Chief Michael Baker.
"An individual that is willing to take action when some folks would not take action. I mean, those are values that the Tulsa Fire Department, you know, espouses as it serves the community," said Baker.
Back in July, the mood was very different. Emerson and his friend were mountain biking at Turkey Mountain when his friend crashed and suffered a serious leg injury.
Despite having no formal first aid training, Emerson stayed calm, called 911 and clearly described his location on the trails.
"I was able to get him up against the tree and sat down, and that leg kind of stabilized, which helps,” said Emerson. “As soon as it happened, I knew that this was probably more serious than I thought it was going to be."
Firefighters praise calm response That composure helped Tulsa Fire Capt. Kayle Greiman and his crew reach them quickly.
"You kept your wits about you, you gave us great directions, and you just did an outstanding job," said Greiman.
Rare honor for young hero At the ceremony, Baker also presented Emerson with one of the department’s limited 125th Anniversary Challenge Coins, a rare honor among firefighters.
Emerson’s father, Matt Kuykendall, is also a Tulsa firefighter and said watching his son step up in a crisis meant a lot to him.
"He was the right person to be there, and so I'm very proud of him," said Matt.
Firefighters said Emerson would make a great firefighter himself one day, and that the Letter of Commendation could help if he applies. Emerson said he just might.
The Tulsa Fire Department said it responds to Turkey Mountain several times each year. They encourage trail users to know their location and carry a phone in case of emergency.
Sam Carrico Sam Carrico is an Emmy Award-winning multimedia journalist who joined the News On 6 team in 2021.
